text: Remove the raised key platforms. Keep the four keycaps close in height to the touch surface; a tiny difference is acceptable. Preserve the actual cap, socket and contact assembly paths.
The earlier five-key layout was replaced by four outer keys and one centre mouse switch.
Keep the key holder as low as possible while preserving its stability.

Leave hand access to insert the bottom-row prewired black sockets and press the switch contacts home beneath the guard. Route the guard supports down first. Preserve the individually accessible switch orientations.
Rotate the bottom key mounting holes 180 degrees to clear the backing socket’s insertion path.
Orient the two-key row at the top and the three control positions at the bottom. Align the centre click with its neighbouring lower keys.
Keep adjacent keycaps as close as practical in both directions without touching or causing neighbouring presses. Using the keys should avoid unwanted rotation of the rod.
A gentle curve between the key rows was suggested as a visual treatment, subject to printability.
Deliver all four key openings, OP1 mounting passages and the hinge insertion line open in the actual slice and usable after printing. Keep internal supports out of these assembly paths.
On the obstructed side, orient the key contacts toward the outer edge so the prewired black socket can be fitted by hand. Preserve the accessible orientation beside the OP1.
Use the actual low-profile Choc V1 switches and keycaps. Retain them locally while allowing removal, swapping and fitting after soldering outside the carrier.
Bring the upper and lower rows as close together as real caps, sockets and prewired assembly access allow. Reduce finger travel without adjacent presses. Use the same centre spacing on both banks.
One printed holder had its functional openings filled. A successfully exported solid or slicer view alone cannot establish that the physical openings are usable.
An earlier printed carrier curled down toward the hinge end and an upper key opening appeared to narrow. The cause was not established.
Remove unnecessary semicircular openings between the keys on the top surface. Retain openings that are required for actual switch or socket insertion and explain any such retained feature.

Keep only the underside openings the actual keys and their black sockets need. Check the switch body, moulded posts, metal contacts, socket bosses, soldered wires and complete installation route before filling unused holes. Make unused ledges and ridges flush with the surrounding underside, including those left by older guard and battery features.

Turn the affected lower key and its prewired black socket back a quarter turn anticlockwise looking from underneath. Retain side access for fitting that socket, keep the opposite bank accessible, and make the two long finger forks match.
